title: How Automatic Transmission Fluid Cooling Works
introduction: I picture the transmission cooler as a heat handoff: fluid brings the heat out of the gearbox, and passing air carries it away. This overview covers vehicles equipped with an automatic transmission and explains the cooler's location and fluid route. It does not specify fluid selection, filling, testing or cooler replacement.

edits.text: Vehicles equipped with an automatic transmission have an external oil-to-air transmission fluid cooler mounted in front of the radiator. Transmission fluid travels from the transmission through the cooler and returns to the transmission through transmission fluid cooler tubes. As ambient air passes over the cooler, heat transfers from the transmission fluid to that air.
edits.why: I separate the fluid route from the heat route: the fluid returns to the transmission, while the surrounding air carries away its heat. The position in front of the radiator identifies the cooler's location; the cooling medium described here is air.
